_comment: The cast and locations a :::dialogue may name. tools/build.py validates every
speaker, every emotion and every background slug against this file and fails
on one it does not know — a dialogue that names an avatar nobody drew would
ship as a broken image beside a speech bubble.
This file declares what EXISTS as a design. The image files themselves arrive
separately; tools/check_cast.py reports which are still missing and does not
fail, so the dialogues can be authored before the art is drawn.
Emotions are deliberately six and shared by every character. A per-character
set would be more expressive and would also mean nobody could ever remember
which ones a given character has. Six x five is thirty avatars, which is a
set one person can actually draw and keep consistent.
An avatar is HALF-BODY, cropped at the waist, not a headshot: two of the five
characters carry their identifying feature on the body rather than the face
(Ba Sau's forearms, Khoa's notebook), and the clothes and build are where
most of the characterisation in this style lives.
ONE FILE PER CHARACTER, not one per emotion. The generated sheet IS the
asset: six panels in a row, saved whole as <slug>.png, and the page shows one
panel by offsetting it. That removes the cutting step, which was the most
error-prone part of the pipeline — six files that had to share a width, a
height and a baseline or the character jumped between lines. It also takes
the cast from thirty files to five.
`col` is the panel's position in the sheet and is therefore LOAD-BEARING:
it is the offset the page uses. It must match the left-to-right order the
prompt asks for. Reordering these without regenerating the art silently
gives every character the wrong face.
research/story/illustration-prompts.md is where these are drawn from, and the
slugs here are the filenames it tells you to save.

sheet._comment: The sheet is one 16:9 image of `cols` equal panels, so a panel is aspect/cols wide for its height. The page derives the crop from these two numbers alone.

neutral.is: Talking, unremarkable. The default, and the one used most.

happy.is: Pleased, warm, amused. A real smile.

worried.is: Anxious or concerned — brows up and together.

annoyed.is: Cross, exasperated, digging in. Brows down.

surprised.is: Caught out, startled. Eyes wide, mouth open.

Thảo.who: his friend, the one who believes him

Khoa.who: top of everything, and kind about it

Mun.who: the black cat; speaks in the passages, not yet in a dialogue

backgrounds.canal-landing: The wooden landing on the canal — mud, water hyacinth, the far bank hazy
backgrounds.kitchen: Bà Sáu's kitchen — low table, enamel bowls, a doorway of hot white light
backgrounds.school-yard: The school yard — concrete, a painted noticeboard, a flame tree
backgrounds.market: The market — stalls, baskets, everyone talking at once
backgrounds.lane: The narrow lane between the houses, evening, light from open doorways
backgrounds.canal-school: The canal behind the school — brown water, a workshop pipe on the far bank
backgrounds.science-room: The school science room after hours — desk lamp, wires, a darkening window
backgrounds.storm-yard: The yard under a storm sky — wind in the banana leaves, water rising
backgrounds.road: The dirt road out of town at first light, the river beyond
